explanation: The remainder theorem says you don't have to do the whole division to find the remainder of f(x) ÷ (x − k): just evaluate f(k). Slide k and the pink dot rides the curve to the height f(k) — that exact height IS the remainder. Change the coefficients a, b, c and the parabola reshapes, but the dot always sits at f(k), so the dashed line over to the y-axis shows the remainder value directly.
bullets: The remainder of f(x) ÷ (x − k) is simply f(k) — one evaluation, no division.
Geometrically, f(k) is the height of the curve directly above x = k.
If f(k) = 0 the remainder is zero, so (x − k) divides f exactly.
